Climate Workbench (Windows, offline)
====================================

Everything runs on this computer. No account, no server, no internet needed
for the bundled datasets.

START THE WORKBENCH
  1. Extract this whole folder (climate.exe, the data folder, the .bat).
  2. Double-click  "Start Climate Workbench.bat".
  3. Your browser opens http://127.0.0.1:8080 .
  4. Keep the "Climate Workbench" console window open while you use it.
     Closing that window stops the server; that is not a crash.

COMMAND LINE
  Open Command Prompt in this folder, then for example:

    climate.exe ui --port 8080
    climate.exe query "is the arctic changing?" --data data
    climate.exe analyze --file data/sst_monthly.csv --variable sst --units degC
    climate.exe help

  Running climate.exe with no arguments prints this help and stays open.

FETCHING REAL DATA (NO ACCOUNT NEEDED)
  Open the "Fetch data" tab and press a source:

    GISTEMP        global temperature anomaly, 1880-present
    POWER          any latitude/longitude, monthly, 1981-present
    NSIDC sea ice  monthly extent, north or south, 1978-present

  These three are open: no login, no Python, no install. The program asks
  Windows' built-in curl for the file, writes data/live_*.csv plus a JSON
  record of the URL and retrieval time, and the analysis runs on it.

  Only Earthdata granule downloads need a NASA Earthdata Login; that is the
  one path that uses the optional Python helper.

IF SOMETHING GOES WRONG
  The program does not close silently on an error. It prints the message, or
  the exception code and address if it fails outside C++ error handling, and
  waits for a key press. Send that text on.

WHAT IT IS
  A single C++17 binary that serves the workbench page and does the science:
  STL decomposition, Mann-Kendall with Hamed-Rao correction, Sen slope, the
  accuracy-weighted estimator ensemble, the polyharmonic CO2 fit, spatial
  hotspot statistics and a registry of 944 executable formulas. The selected
  variable decides which of those formulas run.
